title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: single changepoint detection method dominates across signal shapes, noise regimes, computational budgets: large-scale evaluations find ranking algorithms highly dataset-dependent default configurations often far optimal (van den Burg Williams 2020; Truong et al. 2020). Sound practice therefore requires running several detectors, comparing outputs, — ground truth available — scoring well-defined accuracy metrics. article presents comparison evaluation toolkit ggchangepoint: visual comparison across methods (ggcpt_compare()), common tidy representation competing segmentations (ggcpt_compare_table()), metrics module implementing precision/recall/F1 one--one matching, covering metric, Hausdorff distance, adjusted Rand index (cpt_metrics()), multi-annotator scoring style Turing Change Point Dataset benchmark (cpt_metrics_annotated()), visual evaluation ground truth (ggcpt_eval()). discuss three complementary tools quantifying uncertainty segmentation — engine-native confidence intervals, bootstrap stability profiles (cpt_stability()), CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops()) — close small simulation-based benchmarking workflow built package’s ground-truth generators.

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: changepoint literature offers wide menu detectors — penalised optimal partitioning, binary segmentation wild narrowest--threshold refinements, moving-sum statistics, nonparametric divergence measures, Bayesian posteriors — inductive bias (Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017; Truong et al. 2020). Benchmarks score many algorithms many series find uniform winner: performance depends kind change (mean, variance, distribution), noise (Gaussian, heavy-tailed, autocorrelated), number spacing changes, tuning penalties thresholds (van den Burg Williams 2020). Two practical consequences follow. First, analyst compare several methods data hand rather trust one default. Second, ground truth (expert annotation) exists, comparison quantitative, using metrics agreed conventions. ggchangepoint supports activities behind one interface. Every detector returns tidy ggcpt object, competing methods directly comparable; comparison module renders side side, evaluation module scores . article package’s methods-paper treatment workflow. companion vignette vignette("introduction", package = "ggchangepoint") documents full detection surface; take detectors given focus comparison, evaluation, uncertainty.

title: The ggchangepoint Feature Tour: A Complete Map of the Package Surface
text: Multiscale inference confidence. smuce_wrapper() implements SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014), bounds probability -estimating number changes level alpha returns confidence interval every changepoint location (ci_lower/ci_upper); family = "hsmuce" switches heteroskedastic extension HSMUCE (Pein et al. 2017), estimates variance per segment: Change slope. cpop_wrapper() performs exact penalised estimation continuous piecewise-linear mean (Fearnhead et al. 2019; Fearnhead Grose 2024): Bayesian detection. bcp_wrapper() implements Barry–Hartigan product-partition model (Barry Hartigan 1993; Erdman Emerson 2007); bocpd_wrapper() runs Bayesian online changepoint detection run-length posterior (Adams MacKay 2007); beast_wrapper() wraps BEAST Bayesian model-averaging ensemble (Zhao et al. 2019). first third keep locations whose posterior probability clears prob_threshold record posterior_prob column; BOCPD returns maximum posteriori changepoint set. Sequential kernel nonparametrics. cpm_wrapper() runs distribution-free sequential tests reports, alongside estimated location, detection_time stream monitor flagged (Ross 2015); kcp_wrapper() applies kernel change point analysis running statistics (mean, variance, autocorrelation, correlation) (Arlot et al. 2019; Cabrieto et al. 2018); npmojo_wrapper() detects distributional changes serial dependence (McGonigle Cho 2025): Robustness drift dependence. decafs_wrapper() detects abrupt changes signal also drifts noise autocorrelated (Romano et al. 2022); sn_wrapper() segments chosen parameter (mean, variance, autocorrelation, bivariate correlation) self-normalisation, avoiding long-run variance estimation entirely (Zhao et al. 2022); envcpt_wrapper() reports changepoints changepoint model beats trend autoregressive alternatives (Beaulieu Killick 2018): High-dimensional multivariate. wrappers take matrix data frame one row per time point. inspect_wrapper() finds sparse mean changes projection (Wang Samworth 2018); ocd_wrapper() monitors high-dimensional stream online (Chen et al. 2022); geomcp_wrapper() maps observation distance angle segments (Grundy et al. 2020); multivariate ecp input flows cpt_detect() unchanged. univariate wrappers, contrast, reject multi-column argument rather silently flattening . Regression structure. strucchange_wrapper() dates Bai–Perron breaks, either bare series coefficients formula (Bai Perron 1998, 2003; Zeileis et al. 2002); segmented_wrapper() fits continuous broken-line regression, change reports kink trend rather jump level (Muggeo 2003, 2008). carry confidence interval every break: modern PELT family. fastcpd_wrapper() exposes fastcpd engine, whose family argument covers changes mean, variance, , well changes fitted AR/ARMA/GARCH model (Li Zhang 2024):
code: res_smuce <- smuce_wrapper(x, alpha = 0.5) tidy(res_smuce) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1   100    0.369      100      100 y_slope <- cumsum(c(rep(0.4, 100), rep(-0.3, 100))) + rnorm(200) res_cpop <- cpop_wrapper(y_slope) tidy(res_cpop) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100     39.5 res_bcp <- bcp_wrapper(x, seed = 1) tidy(res_bcp) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value posterior_prob #>   <int>    <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369              1 res_bocpd <- bocpd_wrapper(x) tidy(res_bocpd) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 res_beast <- beast_wrapper(x, seed = 1) tidy(res_beast) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value posterior_prob #>   <int>    <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369              1 tidy(cpm_wrapper(x, cpm_type = "Mann-Whitney")) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>      cp cp_value detection_time #>   <int>    <dbl>          <int> #> 1    23   -1.39              30 #> 2    50    0.426             67 #> 3   100    0.369            104 tidy(kcp_wrapper(x, running_stat = "mean", nperm = 100, seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   101     7.22 tidy(npmojo_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 #> 2   122    8.13 tidy(decafs_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 tidy(sn_wrapper(x3, parameter = "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100   -0.100 #> 2   199    5.53 res_env <- envcpt_wrapper(x, models = c("mean", "meancpt", "trendcpt")) tidy(res_env) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369 res_env$penalty$type   # criterion and winning model #> [1] "AIC: meancpt" set.seed(1) X <- cbind(a = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, 4)),            b = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, -3)),            c = rnorm(160)) res_hd <- inspect_wrapper(X) tidy(res_hd) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>      cp cp_value strength #>   <int>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1    80   -0.590     30.8 # Online detection: the reported locations are declaration times (the change # plus the detection delay), in a `declared_at` column. Monte Carlo threshold # calibration makes this the slowest wrapper, so it is shown but not run # here. It needs at least two coordinates and rejects a univariate series. res_ocd <- ocd_wrapper(X, mc_reps = 100) tidy(res_ocd) tidy(geomcp_wrapper(X)) #> # A tibble: 0 × 2 #> # ℹ 2 variables: cp <int>, cp_value <dbl> tidy(cpt_detect(X, method = "ecp", seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1    80   -0.590 tidy(strucchange_wrapper(x)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1   100    0.369       99      101 tidy(segmented_wrapper(y_slope, npsi = 1, seed = 1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>      cp cp_value ci_lower ci_upper #>   <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> #> 1   100     39.5       98      101 tidy(fastcpd_wrapper(x, family = "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1   100    0.369

code: path <- cpt_crops(x3) path #> ggcpt_path (CROPS penalty path) #>   Change in:       mean  #>   Penalty range:  [5.704, 57.04] #>   Series length:   300  #>   Distinct segmentations: 5  #>  #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   penalty n_cpts  cost #>     <dbl>  <int> <dbl> #> 1    6.69      2  327. #> 2    6.27      5  307. #> 3    6.19      8  288. #> 4    5.76      9  282. #> 5    5.70     10  276. tidy(path) #> # A tibble: 5 × 4 #>   penalty n_cpts  cost cpts       #>     <dbl>  <int> <dbl> <list>     #> 1    6.69      2  327. <int [2]>  #> 2    6.27      5  307. <int [5]>  #> 3    6.19      8  288. <int [8]>  #> 4    5.76      9  282. <int [9]>  #> 5    5.70     10  276. <int [10]> autoplot(path)                          # the cost elbow autoplot(path, type = "path")           # changepoints vs penalty autoplot(path, type = "segmentations")  # the candidate models themselves

title: The ggchangepoint Feature Tour: A Complete Map of the Package Surface
text: autoplot() renders ggcpt. Options: show_segments (fitted segment means), show_fit (engine’s fitted signal, provided — SMUCE, DeCAFS, CPOP, segmented, bcp, BEAST), show_ci (changepoint-location confidence intervals, provided — SMUCE/HSMUCE, strucchange, segmented), show_points/show_line, index date axis, cptline_* styling arguments (cptline_color, cptline_alpha, cptline_type, cptline_linewidth). Asking overlay result supply warns rather failing silently.   Multivariate results facet automatically:  composable layers work inside ggplot pipeline: geom_changepoint() draws vertical rules, geom_cpt_segment() draws segment levels, geom_cpt_ci() draws horizontal interval whiskers, stat_changepoint() runs detection inside plot. theme_ggcpt() publication theme annotate_segments() shades alternating segments.    ggcptplot() ggecpplot() original one-call plots two classical engines:   Bayesian engines get field’s signature displays: ggcpt_posterior() shows posterior mean series per-location changepoint probability (bcp BEAST results); ggcpt_runlength() shows BOCPD run-length posterior heatmap.   Finally, ggcpt_interactive() turns result (ggplot built one) plotly widget values hover. widget embedded , class:
code: autoplot(res, show_segments = TRUE, cptline_color = "firebrick",          cptline_type = "dashed", cptline_linewidth = 0.8) autoplot(res_smuce, show_ci = TRUE, show_fit = TRUE) autoplot(res_hd) cp_tbl <- tidy(res) df <- data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x)  ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   annotate_segments(cp = cp_tbl$cp, n = length(x)) +   geom_line() +   geom_changepoint(data = cp_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "red") +   geom_cpt_segment(     data = res$segments,     aes(x = start, xend = end, y = param_estimate, yend = param_estimate),     inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "darkred", linewidth = 1   ) +   theme_ggcpt() ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   stat_changepoint(method = "pelt", color = "blue") ci_tbl <- tidy(res_smuce) ci_tbl$y_pos <- min(x) - 1 ggplot(df, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line(color = "grey60") +   geom_cpt_ci(     data = ci_tbl,     aes(y = y_pos, xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper),     width = 0.6, color = "blue", inherit.aes = FALSE   ) +   geom_changepoint(data = ci_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "blue") ggcptplot(x, change_in = "mean", cp_method = "PELT") ggecpplot(x, algorithm = "divisive", seed = 1) ggcpt_posterior(res_bcp) ggcpt_runlength(res_bocpd) class(ggcpt_interactive(res))   # requires plotly #> [1] "plotly"     "htmlwidget"

text: cpt_simulate() (alias rcpt()) generates series known changepoints mean, variance, , slope, Gaussian, Student-t, AR(1), random-walk noise; truth travels data true_changepoints true_segments attributes. Five canonical test signals literature ship ready-made: signal_blocks() (Donoho–Johnstone blocks signal (Donoho Johnstone 1994)), signal_fms(), signal_mix(), signal_teeth(), signal_stairs().
code: sim <- cpt_simulate(300, changepoints = c(100, 200), change_in = "mean",                     params = c(0, 5, 1), seed = 1) attr(sim, "true_changepoints") #> [1] 100 200 sim2 <- rcpt(300, changepoints = 150, params = c(0, 3), seed = 2)  # the alias attr(sim2, "true_changepoints") #> [1] 150  signals <- list(blocks = signal_blocks(1024, seed = 1),                 fms    = signal_fms(500, seed = 1),                 mix    = signal_mix(500, seed = 1),                 teeth  = signal_teeth(400, seed = 1),                 stairs = signal_stairs(500, seed = 1)) vapply(signals, function(s) length(attr(s, "true_changepoints")), integer(1)) #> blocks    fms    mix  teeth stairs  #>     11      7      5      3      9 blocks <- signals$blocks ggplot(blocks, aes(index, value)) +   geom_line(color = "grey50") +   geom_vline(xintercept = attr(blocks, "true_changepoints"),              color = "blue", linewidth = 0.3) +   labs(title = "The blocks test signal with its true changepoints")

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: ggchangepoint provides unified, tidy interface changepoint detection across methodological spectrum. introduces single S3 result class, ggcpt, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()) (Robinson 2017), central dispatcher cpt_detect() covering 31 detection methods across six algorithmic families, native ggplot2 (Wickham 2016) visualisation autoplot() set composable geoms. method quantifies uncertainty — simultaneous confidence intervals SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014), break-date intervals Bai–Perron (Bai Perron 1998), posterior distributions Bayesian detectors (Barry Hartigan 1993; Adams MacKay 2007) — result object carries uncertainty plotting layer can draw . package supplies penalty-path diagnostic (CROPS), batch detection panels series, bootstrap stability diagnostics, accuracy metrics aligned current benchmarking conventions (van den Burg Williams 2020), ground-truth simulation, per-method citations. article sets statistical background, design package, method family turn, worked examples throughout.

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: Changepoint analysis — locating instants stochastic behaviour ordered sequence changes — one oldest problems statistics, dating back least continuous-inspection schemes Page (1954), one active: recent surveys catalogue dozens methods (Truong et al. 2020; Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017). applications span virtually every domain produces sequential data, including genomics (Picard et al. 2005), finance (Athey et al. 2022), climate science (Haslett Raftery 1989), signal processing (Lavielle 2005). R ecosystem mirrors breadth. Penalised optimal partitioning lives changepoint (Killick Eckley 2014) fpop (Maidstone et al. 2017); wild binary segmentation wbs breakfast (Fryzlewicz 2014, 2020); multiscale inference stepR (Frick et al. 2014); Bayesian analysis bcp (Erdman Emerson 2007) ocp (Adams MacKay 2007); structural breaks strucchange (Zeileis et al. 2002); . packages excellent , returns different object, follows different indexing convention, draws (draw) plots. analyst wants compare PELT segmentation Bayesian posterior multiscale confidence set — routine task applied work — must therefore learn several APIs, reconcile several conventions, write custom plotting code . ggchangepoint removes friction. design goals : One vocabulary. single front door, cpt_detect(x, method, change_in, penalty, ...), whose arguments mean thing every engine. One result type. Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tidy contract, whatever upstream engine returned. One rendering path. Every result — point estimates, confidence intervals, fitted signals, posteriors, penalty paths — draws autoplot() extends ordinary ggplot2 layers. Wrap, don’t reinvent. detection delegated peer-reviewed upstream engines; optional engines live Suggests loaded requested.

title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: complementary family locates changepoints scanning test statistics. Binary segmentation (Scott Knott 1974; Vostrikova 1981) recursively splits series maximal CUSUM statistic; wild binary segmentation (Fryzlewicz 2014) successor WBS2 (Fryzlewicz 2020) draw random subintervals short segments masked; narrowest--threshold () (Baranowski et al. 2019) favours narrowest interval contrast exceeds threshold, generalises cleanly changes slope; MOSUM (Eichinger Kirch 2018) scans moving-sum statistic fixed bandwidth, across range bandwidths; Isolate–Detect (Anastasiou Fryzlewicz 2022) isolates changepoint expanding interval; TGUH (Fryzlewicz 2018) performs tail-greedy bottom-merge. SMUCE (Frick et al. 2014) occupies special place: estimates step function fewest jumps still passes simultaneous multiscale test level α\alpha, delivers confidence intervals every changepoint location — uncertainty statements competitors make. title: ggchangepoint: A Unified Tidy Interface for Changepoint Analysis in R
text: cpt_detect() dispatches method name; cpt_methods() reports every method package knows, engine, can detect, whether engine installed: Requests validated capability matrix: asking mean-engine variance change error legal alternatives named — never silent substitution. Univariate methods likewise refuse multi-column input rather flattening . Penalty semantics differ across engines, cpt_penalty() documents constructs standard values: Two warrant word. "sSIC" strengthened Schwarz criterion k(log⁡n)αk (\log n)^{\alpha}, α=1.01\alpha = 1.01 default (Fryzlewicz 2014) — marginally heavier BIC, criterion search-based engines apply internally. "MBIC" cpt_penalty() returns 0.5(k+1)log⁡n+log⁡(nk)0.5 (k+1) \log n + \log \binom{n}{k}: BIC-type term plus combinatorial cost placing kk changepoints among nn observations. deliberately stronger "BIC", modified BIC Zhang Siegmund (2007), whose penalty 1.5klog⁡n+0.5∑ilog⁡(ℓi/n)1.5 k \log n + 0.5 \sum_i \log(\ell_i / n) depends segment lengths ℓi\ell_i therefore written function nn kk alone; quantity changepoint package computes character penalty "MBIC". title: Combines Changepoint Analysis with ggplot2
text: Detect one call — cpt_detect(x, method = "...") dispatches 50 methods, classic PELT Bayesian online detection, functional data dynamic networks. Tidy everywhere — every method returns ggcpt object, tidy(), glance(), augment(), time index survives round trip. Plot everything — autoplot() draws result: changepoints, confidence intervals, significance regions, fitted signals, posteriors, multivariate facets, (type =) detector’s statistic, solution path scale space. Trust answer — intervals four provenances, honest tests, criteria actually select K, influence sensitivity diagnostics, consensus across methods, benchmark harness. Extend — as_ggcpt() cpt_register_method() bring external detector tidy, plottable grammar. Run cpt_methods() live table engines, installation status capability flags. three engines required — changepoint, changepoint.np ecp; every engine lives Suggests loaded demand, plain install stays light. cpt_install_engines("bayesian") installs whole family .

what: Detection with uncertainty: confidence intervals and posteriors
title: Combines Changepoint Analysis with ggplot2
text: SMUCE (smuce_wrapper(), via stepR) delivers confidence interval every changepoint location; Bai–Perron (strucchange_wrapper()) broken-line regression (segmented_wrapper()) regression breaks. intervals live ci_lower/ci_upper columns render autoplot(show_ci = TRUE) geom_cpt_ci() layer: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-11 Read intervals, just locations: genuine shift pinned single index, spurious early changepoint carries interval nearly hundred observations wide — exactly distinction bare list locations hides. code: labs <- cpt_labels(c(80, 140), c(120, 190), c("one_change", "no_change")) ggplot(data.frame(t = seq_along(x), y = x), aes(t, y)) +   geom_cpt_label(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, fill = change), data = labs) +   geom_line() +   scale_fill_cpt_label() +   theme_ggcpt() cpt_label_error(res, labs) #> cpt_label_error (2 label(s)) #>   correct: 2   false positives: 0   false negatives: 0 #>   total label errors: 0 #>  #> # A tibble: 2 × 7 #>   label_id series start   end change     n_changes status  #>      <int> <chr>  <int> <int> <chr>          <int> <chr>   #> 1        1 <NA>      80   120 one_change         1 correct #> 2        2 <NA>     140   190 no_change          0 correct series <- list(a = c(rnorm(60), rnorm(60, 4)), b = c(rnorm(80), rnorm(80, 2))) labels <- list(a = as_cpt_labels(60, n = 120), b = as_cpt_labels(80, n = 160)) model <- cpt_learn_penalty(series, labels, penalties = c(1, 4, 16, 64, 256)) cpt_detect(series$a, method = "pelt", penalty = model) #> ggcpt (changepoint detection result) #>   Method:         pelt #>   Change in:       mean  #>   Changepoints found: 1  #>   CP convention:   left  #>   Penalty:         Manual = 43.454  #>   Series length:   120  #>  #> Changepoints: #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>      cp cp_value #>   <int>    <dbl> #> 1    60     1.01

Engines differ read penalty, ?cpt_penalty documents convention: One caveat worth knowing. pelt, binseg, segneigh fpop compare penalty raw segment cost detecting change mean: changepoint’s Normal cost assumes noise standard deviation 1, fpop’s lambda penalises residual sum squares directly. series wider noise penalty effectively negligible segmentation shatters — one true changepoint five-sigma jump, pelt returns 1 changepoint sigma = 1 29 sigma = 3 138 sigma = 10. Standardise series (cpt_detect(scale(x)[, 1], method = "pelt")), pass penalty data’s scale, use change_in = "meanvar", estimates variance per segment. Every engine — SMUCE, WBS, , MOSUM, CPOP, DeCAFS, Bayesian nonparametric families — estimates cancels noise scale unaffected. See ?cpt_detect full note.

title: Combines Changepoint Analysis with ggplot2
text: package provides composable ggplot2 layers changepoint visualisation: Colour never channel carrying meaning. scale_colour_cpt() (scale_color_cpt() alias), scale_fill_cpt() scale_linetype_cpt() Okabe-Ito palette used throughout, safe deuteranopia, protanopia tritanopia; scale_colour_cpt_label() matching discrete scale label-error vocabulary. Every autoplot() also carries generated alt text, rendered figure reaches screen reader without author writing anything.
code: library(ggplot2)  # Use geom_changepoint as a standalone layer cp_tbl <- tidy(cpt_detect(x, method = "pelt", change_in = "mean")) ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_changepoint(data = cp_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "red") +   theme_ggcpt()  # Use stat_changepoint to compute and draw changepoints in one step ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   stat_changepoint(method = "pelt", color = "red")  # Shade alternating segments between changepoints ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   annotate_segments(cp = cp_tbl$cp, n = length(x))  # Draw each segment's estimated level with geom_cpt_segment segs <- cpt_detect(x, method = "pelt", change_in = "mean")$segments ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_cpt_segment(data = segs,                    aes(x = start, xend = end,                        y = param_estimate, yend = param_estimate),                    color = "blue", linewidth = 1)  # Draw confidence intervals with geom_cpt_ci (when the engine provides them) cp_ci <- tidy(smuce_wrapper(x)) ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_cpt_ci(data = cp_ci,               aes(x = cp, xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper, y = min(x) - 1))  # Shade an interval that provably contains a change with geom_cpt_region, # and mark known external events with geom_cpt_event ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_cpt_region(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end),                   data = cpt_regions(cpt_detect(x, method = "nsp"))) +   geom_line() +   geom_cpt_event(aes(xintercept = when, label = what),                  data = data.frame(when = 100, what = "policy change"))

title: ggchangepoint: Release Ledger and Development Roadmap
text: 0.5.0 release answers Part II. 0.4.0 closed “enough methods” gap; 0.5.0 closes three left. Inferential: Narrowest Significance Pursuit brings significance regions — intervals guaranteed contain change global level — new regions slot, new geom_cpt_region() layer, cpt_confint() generic unifies four provenances behind one contract, cpt_test() refuses let selection-unadjusted p-value pass adjusted one. Grammatical: detector’s statistic, solution path scale space now first-class objects accessors plots, autoplot(type =) reaches three. Boundary-shaped: time indices (ts/xts/zoo/tsibble data-frame interface), streaming monitors detection-delay accounting, functional data, dynamic networks, covariance VAR changes, real-world event annotation — , highest-leverage item whole roadmap, extension mechanism (as_ggcpt(), cpt_register_method()) lets detector package neither wraps can depend join grammar. Along way cpt_detect() goes 31 50 wired methods, three duplicated method tables collapse one declarative registry, cpt_select() gives package first criterion actually selects, supervised detection arrives learned penalties, cpt_benchmark() runs grid, cpt_power() answers question precede analysis, package gets first visual-regression net. Part 0 ledger; Part II now annotated delivered . ggchangepoint 0.3.0 closed documentation gap 0.2.0 cycle: README introduces every export, dispatcher honest (wired methods offered), cpt_methods() introspection table ships, ggcpt S3 surface complete (summary/as_tibble/.data.frame/format/plot), eleven verified 0.2.0 bugs (B1–B11) fixed. 0.4.0’s brief opposite 0.3.0’s: documentation, methods. Guided literature--CRAN survey (July 2026; §2), ships largest engine wave package’s history — eighteen new wrappers spanning multiscale inference confidence intervals (SMUCE/HSMUCE), exact change--slope (CPOP), CROPS penalty path, Bayesian detection offline online (bcp, BOCPD, BEAST), sequential/nonparametric testing (CPM, kernel running statistics, NP-MOJO), robustness drift, autocorrelation dependence (DeCAFS, self-normalisation, EnvCpt), high-dimensional multivariate detection (inspect, ocd, geomcp), regression breaks (Bai–Perron/strucchange, segmented), modern fastcpd engine (mean/var/ARMA/GARCH) — taking cpt_detect() 13 31 wired methods (§3). Around new engines builds supporting features compound across : uncertainty-aware plotting (show_ci, show_fit, posterior run-length displays), genuine multivariate input faceted rendering, panel/batch detection, bootstrap stability diagnostics, interactive rendering, per-method citations (§4). also fixes eighty-six verified bugs across three audit passes (§5) — including ecp wrapper fabricated changepoints -change data, WBS wrapper silently discarded model selection claimed use, metrics punished correct “changepoints” answer, hsmuce path terminated R session rather raising error. two commitments define package unchanged: () every detector returns tidy tibble inside structured ggcpt object, (ii) every result directly renderable ggplot2. 0.4.0 adds third: (iii) method quantifies uncertainty — confidence intervals, posterior probabilities, run-length distributions — ggcpt object carries autoplot() can draw . Part II asks comes . “enough methods” gap closed, remaining gaps inferential (package can draw confidence interval engine supplies one, general answer “changepoint real?”), grammatical (visualization-first package draw test statistic, solution path, scale space, changepoint--interval leaving specialty table), boundary-shaped (everything outside bare numeric vector: dates, streams, functional data, networks, external detectors, real-world events). Part II CRAN-verified survey gaps fourteen themes API-level proposals , ordered six waves. read document. Part ledger — decisions already made code already written. Part II design literature document: changelog, commitment. Provenance. Part II maintained separate features.md catalogue (July 2026) merged re-verified 0.4.0 source. Seven proposals turned already implemented, rest claim code longer true. recorded §8.3 removed themes rather left standing work. features.md longer exists; file single roadmap.

title: ggchangepoint: Release Ledger and Development Roadmap
text: nine-area literature--CRAN sweep (penalised/optimal, multiscale, nonparametric/kernel, Bayesian, high-dimensional, regression breaks, online/sequential, robust/dependence, recent benchmarking work, 2020–2026) run July 2026 every citation CRAN status verified. actionable conclusions: Confidence statements now table stakes. SMUCE (Frick, Munk Sieling, 2014) HSMUCE (Pein, Sieling Munk, 2017) give simultaneous confidence sets; Bai–Perron (strucchange) segmented give break-date CIs. visualisation-first package draw interval around changepoint behind field. Bayesian pillar mandatory. Barry–Hartigan (bcp), BOCPD (Adams MacKay, 2007; ocp), widely used BEAST ensemble (Rbeast) CRAN produce field’s signature graphics (posterior profiles, run-length heatmaps) — exactly package’s remit. Slope changes deserve exact engine. cpop (Fearnhead, Maidstone Letchford, 2019; JSS software paper 2024) CRAN canonical answer change_in = "slope" request 0.3.0 route ’s contrast. fastcpd notable newcomer. Li Zhang’s fastcpd (2024) reached CRAN 1.0.0 2026 covers mean/variance/GLM/ARMA/GARCH families one PELT-style interface — survey’s highest-priority “new package miss”. Dependence-aware methods prevent classic false positive. DeCAFS (drift + AR noise), SNSeg (self-normalisation), EnvCpt (changepoints vs trends vs memory), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar, nonparametric serial dependence) CRAN address common practical failure naive mean-shift detection. CRAN availability rules 0.3.0 plans — fewer first thought. gfpop removed CRAN (2024) remains GitHub-; robseg FOCuS never CRAN. None three can live Suggests CRAN package, deferred cpt_methods() says honestly. hdbinseg exception: archived 0.3.0 plan written, refresh found 1.0.3 (Cho) live CRAN , sbs waits wrapper archive — planned_methods() records exactly distinction ("next release" versus "CRAN"). bcp cpm CRAN mid-2026 (brief archival episodes historically; pin versions recurs). covering/F1 one--one matching benchmark standard — audit (§5.1, C12–C15) shows 0.3.0 metrics module implemented inconsistently.

title: Sequential change point model wrapper (CPM) — cpm_wrapper

Distribution-free: "Mann-Whitney" (location, default), "Mood" (scale), "Lepage", "Kolmogorov-Smirnov", "Cramer-von-Mises". Parametric: "Student", "Bartlett", "GLR" (Gaussian), "Exponential" (positive data), "FET" (Fisher's exact test, 0/1 Bernoulli data — one also needs lambda value passed ..., e.g. lambda = 0.3). arl0 Target -control average run length (many observations, average, false alarm). Defaults 500. cpm ships thresholds 100, 200, 370, 400, 500, 600, 700, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000 20000; value refused, engine answers printing error reporting changepoints. startup Number observations restart monitoring begins. Defaults 20. ... Additional arguments passed cpm::processStream().

title: Unified changepoint detection dispatcher — cpt_detect
text: "pelt", "binseg", "segneigh" "fpop" compare penalty raw segment cost change_in = "mean": changepoint's Normal cost assumes noise standard deviation 1, fpop's lambda absolute penalty residual sum squares. Three ways avoid , order convenience: standardise series first     (cpt_detect(scale(x)[, 1], method = "pelt")); pass penalty data's scale, example     penalty = 2 * log(length(x)) * stats::var(diff(x)) / 2; use change_in = "meanvar", estimates variance per     segment unaffected. engines unaffected: SMUCE, WBS, WBS2, , MOSUM, Isolate-Detect, TGUH, CPOP, DeCAFS Bayesian, nonparametric multivariate methods estimate cancel noise scale internally, return segmentation whatever units.

title: Construct changepoint penalties — cpt_penalty
text: penalty name may interpreted differently different engines: changepoint-based methods (PELT, BinSeg, SegNeigh, AMOC):     accept character penalties ("MBIC", "BIC", "AIC",     "Hannan-Quinn", "None") pass upstream     changepoint package. numeric penalty translated     package's penalty = "Manual" plus pen.value. one     exception Segment Neighbourhood, changepoint     implement MBIC: cpt_detect(method = "segneigh")     cpt_wrapper(cp_method = "SegNeigh") therefore fall back     "SIC" default penalty left place, segneigh     result directly penalty-comparable PELT one. Pass     penalty explicitly pin . change mean     engines also read penalty data's scale rather     standardised one; see scale-sensitivity section     cpt_detect. Functional-pruning methods (fpop, cpop,     decafs): accept numeric penalties . character penalty     supplied via cpt_detect(), resolved numeric value     using cpt_penalty() dispatch. Search-based methods (WBS, WBS2, , MOSUM, IDetect,     TGUH): use internal model-selection criteria (e.g., sSIC, threshold)     generally ignore penalty argument. Specify     thresholds via wrapper's arguments. Inference/Bayesian methods (smuce, bcp,     bocpd, beast, cpm, sn): tuned     significance level, posterior-probability threshold, hazard,     average run length rather penalty; see wrapper. MBIC cpt_penalty() BIC-type penalty     adds combinatorial term number ways k     changepoints can placed n observations,     \(0.5(k+1)\log n + \log{n \choose k}\). deliberately stronger     "BIC". modified BIC Zhang     Siegmund (2007), whose penalty     \(1.5 k \log n + 0.5 \sum_i \log(l_i / n)\) depends segment     lengths \(l_i\) expressed function     n k alone. Use character "MBIC"     changepoint-based methods get engine's native MBIC.

code: # \donttest{ # A change in *structure*, not in scale: two latent factors drive # different halves of the node set before and after the change. # Deliberately tiny -- this is by far the most expensive engine in the # package (n_runs x n_reps factorisations per candidate split), and the # settings below are chosen to keep the example inside a check budget, # not to detect anything. Use the defaults on real data. set.seed(2026) block <- function(n, cols) {   f <- abs(stats::rnorm(n)) + 0.5   Y <- matrix(abs(stats::rnorm(n * 5)) * 0.2 + 0.1, n, 5)   Y[, cols] <- Y[, cols] + f   Y } Y <- rbind(block(25, 1:2), block(25, 3:5)) fabisearch_wrapper(Y, min_dist = 10, n_runs = 1, n_reps = 4,                    alpha = 0.25, rank = 2) #> Loading required package: foreach #> Loading required package: rngtools #> ggcpt (changepoint detection result) #>   Method:         fabisearch #>   Change in:       network  #>   Changepoints found: 0  #>   CP convention:   left  #>   Penalty:         engine alpha = 0.25  #>   Series length:   50  #>  #> No changepoints detected. # }

title: ggchangepoint package — ggchangepoint-package
text: ggchangepoint provides consistent S3 result class (ggcpt) changepoint detection results, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()), ggplot2 integration via autoplot() composable geoms (geom_changepoint(), geom_cpt_segment(), geom_cpt_ci(), geom_cpt_region(), geom_cpt_label(), geom_cpt_event(), stat_changepoint()), unified dispatcher cpt_detect() reaches fifty methods. **Detection engines.** cpt_detect() dispatches methods cpt_methods(), across nine families: Penalised/optimal: PELT, BinSeg, SegNeigh, AMOC     (changepoint); FPOP (fpop); fast binary segmentation     (binsegRcpp); CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops());     fastcpd (fastcpd, incl. AR/ARMA/GARCH); change--slope via     CPOP (cpop). Multiscale/search: WBS (wbs), WBS2 TGUH     (breakfast), (), MOSUM incl. multiscale     (mosum), Isolate-Detect (IDetect), SMUCE/HSMUCE     confidence intervals (stepR), WBS nonstationary series     (wbsts). Inference: Narrowest Significance Pursuit (nsp),     returns intervals rather points. Nonparametric/kernel: NP (changepoint.np),     E-Divisive/E-Agglo (ecp), kernel running statistics     (kcpRS), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar), sequential CPM (cpm),     self-normalisation (SNSeg), depth ranks     (KWCChangepoint). Bayesian: Barry-Hartigan posterior (bcp), online     BOCPD (ocp), BEAST model averaging (Rbeast),     formula-based regression changepoints (mcp). High-dimensional: sparse projection     (InspectChangepoint), online ocd (ocd), geometric mapping     (changepoint.geo), sparsity-adaptive ESAC Pilliat     (HDCD), covariance, network, VAR     high-dimensional-regression changes (changepoints). Functional network: functional mean covariance     (fChange), NMF-based network structure (fabisearch). Regression, trend season: Bai-Perron breaks CIs     (strucchange), broken-line regression (segmented),     changepoints-vs-autocorrelation model selection (EnvCpt),     drift+AR robust detection (DeCAFS), BFAST season--trend     breaks (bfast). Classical single-change tests: Pettitt, Buishand     SNHT (trend), Taylor's analyzer (ChangePointTaylor). **surrounds detectors.** Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tibble(cp, cp_value) contract, optionally carrying time index, engine confidence intervals, fitted signal, significance regions diagnostics. Around : Inference: cpt_confint() (four provenances, one     contract), cpt_test(), cpt_regions(). Choosing K: cpt_select() (BIC, Zhang-Siegmund     mBIC, AIC, CROPS elbow, cross-validation, stability),     cpt_crops(), cpt_penalty(). Diagnostics: cpt_influence(), cpt_leverage(),     cpt_sensitivity(), cpt_stability(),     cpt_statistic(), cpt_solution_path(),     cpt_scale_space(). Supervised detection: cpt_labels(),     cpt_label_error(), cpt_label_error_curve(),     cpt_learn_penalty(). Choosing method: cpt_recommend(),     cpt_consensus(), ggcpt_compare(). Evaluation: cpt_metrics(),     cpt_metrics_annotated(), cpt_benchmark(),     cpt_datasets(), cpt_load_tcpd(). Streaming: cpt_monitor(), cpt_update(),     alarms(), cpt_replay(), cpt_delay(). Study design: cpt_simulate(), cpt_power(),     cpt_min_detectable(), cpt_scenarios(). Communication: cpt_annotate_events(),     cpt_report(), cpt_gt(), ggcpt_interactive(),     cpt_cite(). Extension: as_ggcpt()     cpt_register_method() bring detectors package     depend grammar.
